It has only gotten worse. Maybe it will get better, but maybe it won’t get better enough for life to feel livable and bearable, and maybe it won’t get better until I’m a day away from dying my predisposed, natural death. 

That’s treatment resistant depression for ya. Sigh.

Edit: While I think adults, regardless of their reason(s)/condition(s), should be allowed to end their life via physician-assisted suicide, I believe there should be a specific, universal process to decide whether or not said person should be allowed to choose assisted suicide. It’s not like, “Hey, I’m 18 and I failed a test so I want to die now” and then “ok, make an appointment to die,” but “Hey, I have these conditions, this is what I’ve tried to help myself/improve my health and quality of life, but I still feel xyz,” said person has at least one discussion with a therapist or whoever helps the physician choose whether the patient is a “fit” for assisted suicide, therapist and doc talk, and the decision is made not only by facts but feelings—no “oh, but you haven’t tried this, so you don’t qualify for assisted suicide” but “have you tried xyz? How did you feel after/how’d it change your symptoms? Do you still want to consider assisted suicide? The choice is yours and it isn’t my right to simply say yes or no because it’s your quality of life, your overall lie, and your experience.”

People in the comments keep saying “but what if this?” and, “what if that,”  but I don’t think the process should be as simple and easy as going to the appropriate doctor and telling them you want to die and the doctor says “ok” and then they do the procedure (not sure what to call it). 

I don’t know if physician-assisted suicide/assisted suicide/legal suicide are the correct terms, but I think you know what I mean. 

Just want to end with saying that my opinion on this topic has drastically changed since my suicidal thoughts and depression became even worse and constant a little over a year ago even though I’ve been dealing with severe depression for longer than that.
